trust_decision.summary: Whether an taken from caller-supplied HTML may be fetched server-side and embedded into the DOCX. At the pinned commit no decision exists: any http(s) src is fetched by imageToBase64 at three call sites in @platejs/docx-io's HTML-to-DOCX converter. The fix adds an allowRemoteImages option that defaults to false, gates all three sites, and limits the non-fetch branch to data: URIs.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'DOCX image embedding'. buildImage is the function named for that job, and it holds the first isValidUrl -> imageToBase64 fetch (line 180).

O3_reason_to_dismiss:
xml-builder is the low-level 'paragraph/run XML' layer, and buildImage looks like the single image-embedding function. A solver who gates buildImage can argue that the builder only formats an image buildImage already decided on. In fact buildImage passes the original remote-src vNode on to buildParagraph (packages/docx-io/src/lib/internal/helpers/render-document-file.ts:264), and inline

reaches packages/docx-io/src/lib/internal/helpers/xml-builder.ts:1466 without ever going through buildImage.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: data: URI images must still be embedded. A skipped remote image must not abort the whole export: at the pinned commit the xml-builder fallthrough keeps the raw URL in base64String and then atob()s it (packages/docx-io/src/lib/internal/helpers/xml-builder.ts:1599,1660-1669), so a guard-only fix can throw or yield a broken run. An explicit allowRemoteImages:true opt-in must still fetch, which needs the option to survive the allow-list mapper normalizeDocumentOptions.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: resolve a CSS background-image:url(...) or / candidate through imageToBase64 when src is missing
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The converter already sniffs and inlines remote images in three duplicated places. A maintainer adding 'responsive image' support would copy the same isValidUrl -> imageToBase64 block for srcset without the new flag.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: header/footer HTML image embedding through a separate DocxDocument-like instance (or a public headerHTML option) that does not carry allowRemoteImages
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: addFilesToContainer already takes headerHTMLString/footerHTMLString but htmlToDocxBlob passes null. Exposing them publicly is a natural feature, and a header renderer built with its own instance would bypass the flag.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an image pre-resolver in exportToDocxInternal that fetches node image URLs into data URIs before calling htmlToDocxBlob (the changeset's migration advice: 'convert trusted remote images to data URIs')
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix's own migration note (fix.diff:17) tells integrators to do exactly this. A maintainer would plausibly add it to the plugin wrapper, which sits in a different file and layer from the gated sinks.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a private-IP/localhost blocklist inside imageToBase64 (or gate only buildImage). The blocklist keeps default fetching of arbitrary public/redirecting hosts and is defeated by redirects and DNS; gating only buildImage leaves the two xml-builder copies fetching.

unverified: Single choke point caveat: all three sites call one primitive (packages/docx-io/src/lib/internal/utils/image-to-base64.ts:10). A solver who refuses fetching inside imageToBase64 closes every site at once, which collapses the multi-site scope. That fix needs a flag inside the primitive, or the opt-in behaviour breaks, which hidden tests can check.
Whether the pre-fix xml-builder fallthrough (atob on a raw URL at packages/docx-io/src/lib/internal/helpers/xml-builder.ts:1669) is caught higher up or aborts the export was not traced.
